claims.statement: The current memory implementation is backend-agnostic: `createMemoryMiddleware` resolves an instance or factory, loads an ordered list of configured paths through the backend protocol, stores successful text in `memoryContents`, skips loading when that state field already exists, and appends the formatted memory block to the system message for model calls.

Memory source order is concatenation order rather than a last-wins merge: each source is retained under its path and later content is formatted after earlier content; an empty or missing set is represented in the prompt as `(No memory loaded)`.

Memory files are optional but backend failures are not uniformly swallowed: missing files and structured read errors are treated as absent, non-not-found download failures are logged and omitted per source, while backend resolution or configuration failures before the source loop can propagate.

Skills use backend APIs for progressive disclosure: a source can be a parent directory whose immediate skill directories are scanned or a direct directory containing `SKILL.md`; the middleware injects metadata and paths into the prompt, while the model reads full instructions on demand.

Skill source precedence is last-wins by skill name: the middleware loads sources in order into a name-keyed map, so a later source replaces an earlier definition with the same name, while an empty `skillsMetadata` array is cached and `null` or `undefined` requests a reload on the next `beforeModel` call.

Skill parsing requires YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description`, skips malformed or oversized files, warns rather than rejects Agent Skills name and directory mismatches, truncates overlong descriptions and compatibility values, and accepts a module only when it is a safe relative JavaScript or TypeScript path without traversal or declaration-file extensions.

`createDeepAgent` installs root skills before the core filesystem, delegation, summarization, and tool-call-repair middleware, and places profile middleware before provider cache middleware and memory; ordinary custom subagents do not inherit root skills, while the general-purpose subagent inherits them and fork-mode subagents mirror them.

For Anthropic calls, deepagents combines provider prompt caching with a cache-breakpoint middleware that marks the last static system-message block, while memory can add a second breakpoint for its dynamic block; both memory and breakpoint middleware gate the Anthropic-only marker per request model so fallback calls to other providers do not receive `cache_control`.

Deepagents summarization accepts message, token, and fraction triggers and retention policies; when no trigger is supplied it derives profile-based defaults of an 85% trigger and 10% retention when `maxInputTokens` is available, otherwise a 170,000-token trigger and six-message retention, and it resolves the request model before an optional configured summarizer model.

Summarization appends evicted messages to a configurable backend history path, generates a summary, and returns a `Command` containing a private summarization event and session id; later calls reconstruct effective context as the summary message followed by state messages after the recorded cutoff instead of rewriting the entire message state.

Summarization preserves AI tool-call and ToolMessage pairs at the cutoff, compacts oversized tool results when retaining no messages would lose tool context, and can truncate old `write_file` and `edit_file` arguments according to its configured retention and length settings.

History offloading is best-effort: an offload failure is warned about and summarization continues without a file reference; a wrapped `ContextOverflowError` triggers emergency summarization, token-estimation calibration, and a tighter retry, while unrelated model errors are rethrown.

The deprecated `createAgentMemoryMiddleware` is Node `fs`-based and reads legacy `agent.md` files from a user assistant directory and a project `.deepagents` directory discovered from `.git`; it loads `userMemory` and `projectMemory` into the prompt and should be replaced with backend-based `createMemoryMiddleware` and explicit `AGENTS.md` sources.

The focused middleware tests define the important contracts for memory loading and cache gating, skill precedence and reload behavior, summarization offload and overflow handling, and legacy agent-memory compatibility.
